messages.subject: [statnet_help] Problems installing on Solaris 10 (intel)
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I tried to do an

install.packages("statnet")

on my Solaris 10 server and started getting lots of errors.

The worst being from degreenet, and latentnet.

Degreenet seems to require gfortran, which I unfortunately am having problems installing under Solaris.

Latentnet throws the following error:
post_utils.c: In function `post_pred_wrapper':
post_utils.c:254: error: wrong type argument to unary minus
*** Error code 1
make: Fatal error: Command failed for target `post_utils.o'

Has anyone else had these problems? I also recall there used to be a precompiled Sun binary, but that was for a much earlier version.

Thanks!
-y

messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

 

I run the same erg model 160 times on different network data sets. In a few
of them, I get an error message. I don't understand what this error message
means. 

Can anyone help me with that?

 

The model is:

 

model283 <- ergm(vlo283 ~ edges + gwesp(0.25, fixed=TRUE) + mutual +
nodematch("klasnr2") + nodematch("alloch2b") + nodematch("OndType") +
nodematch("female") + nodeifactor("alloch2b") + nodeofactor("alloch2b") +
nodeifactor("female") + nodeofactor("female"), verbose = F, MCMCsamplesize =
1000, maxit = 3, control=control.ergm(steplength=0.25))

 

 

The error message is:

 

Error in covar[!is.na(theta) & !m$etamap$offsettheta, !is.na(theta) &  : 

  number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length

In addition: Warning message:

In theta[!m$etamap$offsettheta] <- real.coef :

  number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length

 

 

I also send in this mail the R-code to become "vlo283" so you can try it
yourself.

 

 

Thank you,

 

Jef

messages.subject: [statnet_help] ergm output: std. error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jef,

I think the easiest way to pull out the asymptotic standard errors (the 
ones given in the summary command) is just by typing:

summary(my.ergm.object)$asyse

You can also calcuate them directly without having to invoke the summary 
command if you wish; you can look inside the summary.ergm command to see 
how one might do this.

I imagine it would be useful to have an ergm object include the 
asymptotatic standard errors of the coefficients as one of its elements, 
yes?

Steve

messages.subject: [statnet_help] error in covar[!is.na(theta) & !m$etamap$offsettheta, !is.na(theta) &
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jef.  Mark Handcock noticed that your "female" variable contains  
all zeros, which is causing a couple problems that will be fixed if  
you drop all the "female" terms:

First, it means that nodematch("female") is always equal to "edges"  
for any network.  Thus, you have a problem including both of those  
terms in your model.

Second, it means that nodeifactor("female") and nodeofactor("female")  
don't make sense -- and this is what is actually causing the error.   
In fact, you seem to have found a bug in ergm:  nodeifactor and  
nodeofactor weren't written to be robust enough to deal with calls  
like this in which the user tries to define a factor on a variable  
with only a single value.  Oops!  I'll add this to the to-do list, and  
thanks for the heads up.

Dave

messages.body_plain:
hi statnet team,

i know there are now options available for visualizing dynamic network 
data (e.g. the last article in the special issue of joss)- but does 
statnet offer any way of actually modeling longitudinal data using 
ergms? or is SIENA still the only program available to do this (although 
using a different statistical framework)? in general, i would love to 
hear what other kinds of things we may see in the future of statnet, and 
any thoughts you may have on the longitudinal modeling issue. thanks!

-kevin
